what: DigitalOcean sells cloud computing to developers and small businesses: virtual servers, storage and databases at simple flat prices, without the complexity of the large cloud platforms.
customers: Software developers, startups and small businesses running applications in the cloud.
money: virtual servers, storage, databases and managed services
GPU capacity and AI development tools
moat: Simplicity and price transparency for customers too small to negotiate with Amazon or Microsoft, plus documentation and community that make it the default for independent developers.
risks: 275 times earnings: the reported profit is tiny relative to the valuation
Growth has slowed to around 15% a year
$1.6B of debt against $255M of cash, from convertible notes
opportunities: $244M of free cash flow and a 28.8% operating margin
Revenue grew from $429M to $901M in four years
Analysts see about 108% upside, with 15 covering the stock, and its GPU cloud serves developers the big clouds price out
watch: Revenue growth and net dollar retention, which shows whether customers spend more over time.
